title: The search for meaning is disease
description: It is based on a false premise, that you are incomplete and need to find something to become whole. If you accept that there is no inherent meaning, the mind has no job. It panics. To avoid this horrific silence, you create ideologies and debates about nonsense to keep this psychological engine running. You do not want a solution. You want the endless hunt. Chasing the perfect something or ideological purity gives you a false sense of purpose....

title: Dreams and prayer
description: Brennan tried to be a healer and savior: https://brennan.day/i-m-looking-for-love/ He preaches love as the universal cure while simultaneously advertising his own lack of it. All of this to say that I am, right now, looking for love. I am in a season of yearning! Dreams of an Internet boyfriend/girlfriend. And this post is an embarrassing declaration, as much as it is a genuine prayer.

title: Fantasies
description: Subhumans detected article Defense mechanism activated in one reader. I got an email from Brennan ( https://brennan.day/ ) with the part: But people are trying. They aspire to goodness and principles no matter how badly they perform. That means something. I'd much rather have a virtue-signalling hypocrite that misuses the word "Nazi" than a cynical misanthropic nihilist. Only one actually gives the world a chance, no matter how flawed....

title: Customer acquisition
description: Open source, stand with X, against Y. Moral business owner. Good respectable citizen. Ethical business. Then reality hits a bank account. Somebody used "open source" offered. Audience is on platform Y. The realization, that being morally pure is bad for business. Taking a "stand" generates engagement, press, and loyal followers. When that strategy stops yielding profit, or when the algorithm actively punishes their absence, the "values" are quietly discarded....

title: Politics
description: I am already a victim of over ten elections in Slovakia, as far as I can remember. I haven't voted even once. There is just one pattern I see. No matter who won, things got worse. Heads up, keep morale high, and enjoy your next election. I see the future, it will get worse.

title: Subhumans detected
description: You see that random nobody wrote meaningless 20 words on some online platform. He is like you, but because he uses platform X and not Y, he is a nazi. You have no idea what "nazi" word means. You never used it 5 years ago. Now you "discovered" it. Your group uses it to label everyone who has a different opinion. So you as a smartass have to use it too. Easy, cheap, and it does not require anything. No discussion, argument, or fight. Just a label and the game is over....

title: Closed loop
description: The Intellectual Circle Jerk and Why We Can't Stop https://www.joanwestenberg.com/p/the-intellectual-circle-jerk-and The credentialing cartel. Same top-tier universities, same books, same thinking. If you do not think like them, you do not get the degree. You do not get the internship. You do not get the job. A World Bank economist becomes an EU regulator, then joins a NGO board, then consults for a UN agency. Fact-checking each other to ensure nobody deviates from the approved script....

title: Brand new app icon
description: There is a little genocide in some Africa village. Kids mine some toxic materials by hands for food. Kids die. The new phone is assembled by slaves. People die. You have some opinion about some app icon change or the latest social media post by the CEO. You love it, hate it, you share "your" take. The company does not care. Everything runs as intended.

title: Personal websites
description: Recently it's relatively easy to find out hundreds or even thousands of personal websites online. It was not like that few years ago. The internet was strictly dominated by corporations directly. Now magically "personal" opinions and thoughts are easy to find on the web. It's already safe for the system to allow that. There are almost no personal opinions or thoughts anymore. Everything dangerous was mostly destroyed, edges were sanded and polished....

title: Internet
description: The last time I enjoyed the internet was probably a decade ago. Rushing from a grocery store to turn on my computer and join my online brothers in arms. Load Battlefield 3 and run with a sniper rifle like it's a shotgun. "Aggressive sniping" it was called. I had no idea what FPS meant or what good gaming setup was. I played on random crap I had that time. Like when I was a kid. Wood stick was good for a sword. I was Robin Hood or any other dumbass I saw in a movie. I fought in the garden....

title: Template
description: More I randomly click on the internet, more I see the same template. Topic does not matter. "Who in 2026?" "The last time I listened this song, my father ..." "AI this and that." "I wish the app ..." Pre-programmed desperate reflex. Rarely even opinion or thought. Executed script. Mechanical output of human mind. Free or very cheap.

title: Roll call
description: Idiot challenge, #shitfest, stupidity festival. Post every day, link something, reply to someone, send 100 emails. Every day, every month there is some circus. A man announces a challenge, thirty people link to it, they all post about posting, they link each other's posts about linking. The circle closes. Until next call. Peasant writes because there's something to say. Member who sends 100 emails or writes 100 posts doesn't have 100 things to say....

title: Email
description: On 31/07/2026 2:01 AM, Poetic Knight wrote: How presumptuous of you, and what a dickish tone you either deliberately took or else have as a default. If you read my latest three posts, it culminates with calling Herman out for still applying censor via modifying the post buoyancy....

title: Tone
description: Someone says something true and sharp. The response is never "you're wrong". Never "here's why". Always "your language is inappropriate". The content vanishes. The tone becomes the trial. The person who said the thing is now defending how they said it. The person who did the shit walks free. IRC, fediverse, the office, corporate email, academia. Same script. No argument required. The tone was the crime. Someone gets censored. Their response: "it just felt weird". Not "this is nonsense". Weird....

title: No conspiracy needed
description: Apple's mouse charges face down. Windows removes the 'no' button. The bank holds your money and demands permission. This is hostile design. TSA catches shoes but misses weapons. Government offices demand three copies for a meaningless stamp. This is bureaucratic rot. Neither requires a master plan. Like a mother who uses daily guilt to control her child without a blueprint. The power dynamic is not engineered. It builds itself. You flip the mouse. You strip at checkpoints. You click 'not now'....

title: The bundle
description: You ask for text. Just a few words. They don't sell text. Text is free. So they sell the wrapper. You get HTML, CSS, and two megabytes of JavaScript. Fifty million lines just to render your banana cake recipe. Then the platform. The likes, the comments, the feed from your new tribe. You want an email client. Just send a message. They give you an AI assistant, a calendar, a crypto wallet, and a monthly fee. You want the potholes fixed. But you cannot just buy the asphalt....

title: The cut
description: I get an idea. Few words, a sentence or two. I start writing. After few lines it's clear it's going to be shit, a novel. Explaining, examples, luckily not many metaphors, as my English level does not allow it. The first spit is lazy mode. I talk until everyone falls asleep and I can leave. Done. Mind just keeps going until it feels everything is covered. The second distilled version requires more work. No pressure to be right or understood. No fillers. No saying the same thing three times....

title: I don't care
description: I canceled the OpenBSD server. Moved to free Cloudflare. The infrastructure doesn't matter. I get an extra pack of cigarettes now. I used a feed reader for almost a month. Too long. I killed it. Reading is just consuming other people's vomit. I wrote my thoughts. Sent emails. The spam filter caught it. The machine did its job.

title: Own your content
description: POSSE it, they say. Own your content. Publish once, fork it five times. RSS, Mastodon, Bluesky, webmention, pick your parasite. Fix the typo in two minutes. Already too late. Fossils wearing your name.

title: The cult list
description: POSSE. Webmention. ActivityPub. AT Protocol. Fediverse. IndieWeb. Micro.blog. Bearblog. Pika Pulse. /now page. /uses page. Discovery feed. Own app. Own icon. Own font. Same rats, smaller cage, better lighting.

title: He sleeps fine
description: Killed a man Tuesday. Checked his oil, packed a lunch, drove three hundred miles to do it. The boy looked like his nephew. Same jaw, same stupid haircut. Wednesday he kissed his daughter on the forehead. Told her to be good. Meant it. No animal forgives itself. It just eats and moves on. He needs God, a flag, and a stranger with more stripes. Three lies stacked on a fresh grave. Friday he is at his daughter's recital. Claps loudest.

title: The man
description: AI flooded the internet. Google broke search. Company poisoned the river. Pharma knew, shipped anyway. Parliament voted. Fairy tales. A man did every one of those things. With a name, a face, a paycheck.

title: Your opinion is irrelevant
description: Doctor says six months. Your opinion was five years. Prayer changes nothing. Morphine does. You argue with your father about it anyway. Right up until he stops breathing. You were right. He is dead. Heart stops. No referendum.

title: The fake party
description: A man sits in a chair and shouts because some millionaire kicked or threw a ball. Another waits for a multi-billion corporation to tell him what his phone will do next year. Do people realize it is not real? That it is just business? Simulating missing belonging with a logo on a machine or a t-shirt is a fake party. There is no tribe, just your wallet and attention. You buy the excitement. You pay to feel part of a pack that does not know you exist. This theater is annoying to observe.

title: Simple tools are not popular
description: Simple things, especially in tech, are not popular. Some may be used silently behind the scene, but they are rarely visible or promoted. The reason is simple. It's impossible to create a business around them. You can't create an industry around a plain text file. There are no conferences, books, or presentations about primitive utilities. Those tools are simple, and they work. Nothing exciting. Hard to extract money from it. Complexity is a feature for the people who profit from it....

title: Contact forms
description: Is any channel worse for communication than a contact form? Maybe a postcard when you don't know the address.
